Data Infrastructure: Consolidate the highest-value datasets onto a single governed platform before adding any new source system.
Automate the manual data movement causing the most rework: replace it with a scheduled, monitored pipeline.
Define and test a recovery time objective and recovery point objective for your most critical dataset.
Data Quality and Governance: Assign a named owner to every dataset used in board-level or client-facing reporting.
Stand up automated quality checks (completeness, accuracy, freshness) on your three most-used datasets.
Publish a single governed definition for each core reference entity (customer, product, region) and retire local variants.
Analytics and Reporting: Build a certified metric layer for your top 5 KPIs so every report draws from the same definition and source.
Move your highest-effort recurring report from manual assembly to a scheduled, automated build.
Train a self-service cohort in one business unit and measure their report-request volume before and after.
AI and ML Readiness: Stand up a defined experimentation environment separate from production, even if it starts with a single technical owner.
Document and codify a deployment path for the next model you build, rather than leaving it in a notebook.
Create an intake process that scores AI opportunities against feasibility and business value before any build starts.
Data Culture and Skills: Secure a named executive sponsor for the data function with a defined mandate and budget line.
Run a baseline data literacy assessment and target training at the roles with the largest gap.
Embed a data specialist inside one business unit for a fixed period and track the change in decision quality.
